key_insight: Execution-state capsules extend reuse beyond KV caches by checkpointing and restoring the full graph-bound execution state for low-latency, small-batch on-device AI serving.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, exact branch/reset/rollback behavior for interactive agents, speech, and robot policies without relying on high-throughput KV-cache assumptions.
method: Capture the complete restorable state at a committed graph boundary into a capsule.
Store live state in closed, named contiguous buffers so it can be snapshotted and restored without block-table indirection.
Support restore, fork, and rollback across KV, recurrent, convolution, MTP state, and metadata.
evidence_signal: On RTX 5090, restore is byte-exact and greedy decoding is token-identical; GPU-resident snapshot/restore is sub-millisecond, and TTFT speedup vs cold prefill rises from 3.9x at 2k tokens to 27x at 16k tokens, with results also holding on Jetson AGX Thor and DGX Spark.
watch_item: This approach depends on a white-box runtime and backend-controlled static buffer layout, so portability and integration with existing opaque serving stacks may be nontrivial.
paper_title: Execution-State Capsules: Graph-Bound Execution-State Checkpoint and Restore for Low-Latency, Small-Batch, On-Device Physical-AI Serving
